norcb K=100000 90s wall: vtime_burned=393.46s while guest_ts frozen at 0.0797s (owner's ~400x vtime/guest decoupling, live). turns=122411, su0=108687 (88.8% zero-duration polls), su_future=6439 (future timed waiters DO exist), preempt_events=0 (no burn-out fires under --no-rcb-time). vtime_per_turn=3.21ms.

Need a WEDGED/skid rcbtime run to test H9.

SMOKING-GUN MECHANISM (refined from owner framing). In norcb log the 6439 nonzero SleepUntil targets are NOT stuck far below committed: they track ~74-75ms ahead of current committed and ARE delivered (6439 committed). Consecutive targets step by ~74000000ns=74ms. So the guest is stuck in a ~74ms relative-timeout poll loop (early-boot HPET/timer calibration); Detcore commits each poll-timeout in sequence, inflating committed_time ~74ms/poll (~5300 polls -> 393s vtime) WITHOUT the vCPU thread ever executing the instructions that finish calibration. Future timers DO fire; they are all unproductive epsilon-polls. Correction to 'timer stuck below committed never fired': the decoupling is real (400x) but its form is unproductive-poll-timeout inflation, not a starved-below-committed deadline. rcb-time supplies the missing burn-out: PMU preemption forces vCPU RCB/icount progress between polls. dtid17 busiest (73730 commits) = QEMU main-loop poller.

DECISIVE norcb linearity sweep (--target-timeslice 1e3..1e7, 4 orders of magnitude, 120s wall each). vtime_burned FLAT ~490s +/-4% (494.5,492.4,484.7,507.8,491.5); guest_ts FLAT ~0.71s NEVER escapes at any K; preempt_events=0 at EVERY K. At extreme K=1e7 the knob only coarsens poll granularity (turns 161678->46088, vtime/turn 3.06ms->10.66ms) but total vtime and guest progress UNCHANGED. => INSENSITIVE/non-linear response. --target-timeslice is INERT under --no-rcb-time (installs no productive preemption). H8 CONFIRMED: burn-out mechanism MISSING, spin UNBOUNDED not mistuned. Artifact: debug/demo5-regression/sweep.csv.

rcbtime CONTROL arm (--target-timeslice 1e4..1e6, 150s wall). preempt_events=380/399/435 (>0, burn-out PRESENT) vs norcb 0. Knob RESPONDS: turns 95932->73911->14727, preempt-per-turn 1/252->1/185->1/34, vtime_burned 156.5->149.6->128.2s as K grows (larger slice = fewer longer turns, more logical time per preemption). Contrast is decisive: the ONLY spin-bounding mechanism is 'inbound timer preemption event' which requires PMU/rcb-time; under --no-rcb-time it is absent so no knob bounds the spin. (Partial-wall so neither arm hit ts>=1.8 escape; N=20 rcb batch is the boot ground-truth, 12/20 BOOT_OK ts=1.819.)

P0 PMU-vs-syscall split (source-grounded + log-counted). Demo config demos/05-qemu-boot.py:131-136 = --strict --no-rcb-time --target-timeslice 100000 --max-timeslice disabled. SOURCE (226 code-search): the PMU/RCB timer is armed ONLY when max_timeslice.is_some() (post_handler_hook lib.rs:640-644); 'inbound timer preemption event' (lib.rs:1329) IS the PMU path exclusively; --target-timeslice sets a SOFTWARE syscall-boundary deadline (end_of_timeslice, checked every handler entry), --max-timeslice sets the PMU deadline. So --max-timeslice disabled => max=None => ZERO PMU by construction; preemption 100% at syscall boundaries. LOG COUNTS (PMU='inbound timer preemption event', total='ending timeslice T', syscall-bound=diff): run-bbx-wedgekit (DEMO config, busybox) = 0 PMU / 387451 ends / 387451 syscall-bound / 387450 SleepUntil0 -> 0-PMU AND WEDGES. All full-linux controller archives (run-good-f6c836b1 0/39343, run-broken-ae2565be 0/817815, run-norcb 0/5536314, run-mid-1190 0/223230) = demo config = 0 PMU, all WEDGE. CONTRAST: run-bbx-green (busybox --strict, rcb ON, max=default 200ms) = 858 PMU / 868 ends = 98.8% PMU -> the ONLY genuine boot-to-powerdown, and it is the rcb-time WORKAROUND. PRECISION FIX to H1 prose: bare --no-rcb-time with DEFAULT max still ARMS the PMU (run-bbx-wedge: --no-rcb-time only, max=200ms => 519 PMU events) — it is --max-timeslice disabled, not --no-rcb-time, that zeroes PMU. ANSWER TO OWNER P0: green did NOT depend on PMU at all (0 by construction, small target + disabled max = syscall-boundary regime); PMU-skid is NOT on the green path; the fix is restoring the syscall-boundary regime (fix scheduler-vtime-jump-unproductive-pollers so max-disabled config boots again instead of SleepUntil0 livelock).

H9 route-(b) skid-hunt NEGATIVE under config --target-timeslice 100000 --max-timeslice 200000000: 14/20 rcbtime controller boots (N=20 batch) with 0 skid, 0 non-boot, 0 rearm-failure; healthy runs show 'inbound timer preemption event' continuing to within 1-3 turns of tail. This config does NOT reproduce the ~20% skid (that came from the panic-prone rcb-time-time margin config in demo5-rcb-config-panic-vs-slow-tradeoff). Testing H9 route (b) requires the panic-prone config + 210 turn-order; route (a) (--no-rcb-time, preemption never armed, 0 skid) fully accounts for the demo5 wedge studied here.

H9 FALSE-POSITIVE CORRECTION (adversarial). run-15 & run-16 tripped the naive preempt_timeline signature (preemption ceased 15881 / 97505 turns before log-end, su0 exploding) but BOTH completed BOOT_OK. Cause: at run-16 turn 76208 dtid17 (CPU-bound vCPU poller) took its LAST preemption ('ending timeslice T67680, 0 syscalls this timeslice') then turn 76209 handed off to dtid7 running clock_nanosleep(CLOCK_MONOTONIC,...) — a PHASE TRANSITION from CPU-bound TCG execution to sleep-driven threads. Once the CPU-bound thread stops running RCBs there is nothing to PMU-preempt, so preemption ceases in HEALTHY boots too. Therefore 'preemption ceased before log end' is NOT a valid rearm-failure signature by itself. run-15 preemption RESUMED (last_p 179450->184943) confirming it was sparse, not dead. Valid H9 test requires a run whose FINAL verdict is non-BOOT_OK with dtid17 still the active poller and preemption dead. Under this config (target-timeslice 100000 max-timeslice 200000000): 16/20 BOOT_OK, 0 wedge, 0 skid => route (b) does NOT reproduce here.

Hardened wedge-detector validated: preempt_timeline.sh now attributes the TAIL (commits after last preemption) to a discovered poller dtid and classifies NO-PREEMPT-BY-CONFIG (H8/norcb) / PREEMPTION-ACTIVE / PHASE-TRANSITION / WEDGE-REARM-FAILURE. Validated on 3 known logs: norcb spin -> NO-PREEMPT-BY-CONFIG (preempts=0, su0=138199); rcb SLOW_CENSORED run-17 -> PREEMPTION-ACTIVE (gap=852); rcb SLOW_CENSORED run-18 -> PHASE-TRANSITION (gap=2787 but dominant dtid 9 != poller 17). Confirms E19: the naive 'preemption ceased before end' signature false-positives on healthy handoff (old script would have flagged run-18). WEDGE-REARM-FAILURE branch is untriggered in this never-wedging config and is reserved for 210's route-(b) hunt in the panic-prone margin config.
